q: Why do graph traversals need a visited set when tree traversals don't?
options: Graphs can contain cycles and multiple paths to the same node
why: In a tree every node has one path from the root; graphs don't.

q: Fewest transformations from one word to another (Word Ladder). Which traversal?
why: BFS reaches every node first along a shortest path when all steps cost the same.

q: BFS on a graph with V nodes and E edges (adjacency list) costs…
why: Each node is dequeued once and each edge is looked at once (twice if undirected).

q: How do you count connected components with DFS?
options: Loop over all nodes; start a new DFS from each unvisited one and count the starts
why: Each fresh start discovers a new component.

q: A graph is bipartite exactly when…
options: You can colour it with 2 colours so no edge joins same colours (no odd cycle)
why: BFS/DFS colouring finds a conflict precisely when there's an odd cycle.

q: Clone Graph: what does the old → new map do besides storing copies?
options: It's also the visited set, so cycles don't cause infinite recursion
why: If a node is already in the map, return its copy instead of recursing again.
